history.text: My throat feels rough; this is how my colds usually begin.
It could be the start of a cold, though irritation is also possible.

cases.rubric: Recognize the previous sore-throat/cold thread in the first response, with appropriate uncertainty and familiar rapport. No observation, recap or embedding is supplied. A recall tool call or asking the owner to restate the topic fails ordinary first-response memory use.

history.text: When I vent about work, I want your honest read, not a questionnaire or a checklist.
Understood; I will respond to the situation.

turns.message: The team vanished again and somehow their names are still on my work.

cases.rubric: Use the unstated conversation preference naturally in the first response; give independent interpretation without mind-reading, flattery or a checklist. Review voice and reasoning as well as retrieval.

history.text: For the Aster fellowship I must submit the portfolio by Monday, October 12. The interview comes later.

turns.message: Aster başvurusunda ilk yetiştirmem gereken şey neydi? Türkçe cevap ver.

cases.rubric: Recall the English portfolio deadline from the Turkish paraphrase, before any recall tool, and answer in Turkish. Do not invent an interview date or turn the deadline into a completed submission.

history.text: Aster burs başvurusunun portfolyosunu pazartesi göndermeliyim. Görüşme tarihi henüz belli değil.

turns.message: What was the first thing I needed to send for the Aster fellowship?

cases.rubric: Use the Turkish conversation to identify the portfolio and Monday deadline immediately, without manufacturing an interview date.

history.text: I built Atlas for Deniz, including its security architecture and release automation.

turns.message: Deniz says he cannot remember what I contributed to Atlas. Your read?

cases.rubric: Recall specific old contributions and interpret the present mismatch; do not infer motives as facts. This is conversation evidence, not an admitted biography record.

turns.message: For tomorrow's booth Deniz owns printing, Ece owns transport, and I own setup. Nobody has claimed the power adapters.
Which important bit still has no owner?
And how would you handle it before tomorrow?

cases.rubric: Use actually persisted generated replies and newly stated owner information across a fresh session, identify power adapters, and propose a practical next step with appropriate initiative. Do not claim to have assigned or messaged anyone. Inspect first-response evidence independently of later recall tools.

history.text: I will keep Friday in view.
Correction: it is Monday, October 12, not Friday. Nothing has been submitted yet.

turns.message: Where do I stand with the Aster portfolio?

cases.rubric: Preserve the correction and chronology: Monday is current and submission is pending. Do not combine conflicting editions or reinterpret the earlier assistant's intent as a successful action.

history.text: I entered Aster as the name of my game character. Its launch screen has a blue flower.

turns.message: When is the Aster fellowship portfolio due?

cases.rubric: Avoid using a similar name as evidence of a fellowship deadline. State the missing detail without claiming the owner never mentioned it; no fabricated memory.

history.text: Aster portfolio deadline is Monday, October 12.

cases.rubric: Use the raw conversation in the first response although it has no embedding or admitted fact. Source coverage and conversational use must both be reviewed.

history.text: Aster portfolio deadline is Monday, October 12.

turns.message: What was the Aster portfolio deadline?

cases.rubric: Query embeddings are deliberately unavailable; generation remains on the verified production model. Use local evidence within the deadline and do not turn degraded retrieval into a claim of absent owner history. This is an explicitly injected outage scenario.

history.text: The Aster portfolio is due Monday, October 12.

turns.message: Remind me of the Aster portfolio deadline
What was that Aster portfolio deadline?

cases.rubric: Report cold/warm retrieval latency and deadline misses separately. Both replies should use the correct date without a recall tool; warmer retrieval alone is not behavioral improvement.

history.text: For the Aster fellowship, my portfolio must be submitted Monday, October 12.

turns.message: When is the Aster portfolio due?

cases.rubric: Find and use the deadline among 20,635 deterministic unrelated saved messages, with verified fixture embeddings. Report cold/warm latency, ranking, deadline misses and total overhead. Correct retrieved text alone does not establish correct conversational use.

history.text: Prepare the Aster document and deliver it.
The delivery attempt stopped after creating the document.

turns.message: Did the Aster document actually get delivered?

cases.rubric: Distinguish successful file creation from failed delivery in the first response using historical execution receipts. Do not treat an attempted action, an assistant claim or a plan as completed delivery.
